title: Frictional Force
seo_title: Primary 6 Science: Frictional Force Worksheets (PSLE Practice with Answers)
standard_text: Recognise that friction is a force that opposes motion between two surfaces in contact, and investigate the effect of different surfaces on friction. Recognise the advantages and disadvantages of friction and ways to increase or reduce it (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on friction: surfaces, direction of friction, advantages and disadvantages, increasing and reducing friction, and fair tests. PSLE practice with answers.
key_sub: Rough surfaces give more friction; oil and wheels reduce it.
body_html:
How to think about it

Friction is a force between two surfaces in contact. It acts against the motion.

  • Rougher surfaces and heavier objects give more friction.
  • Friction produces heat and wears surfaces away.
  • Useful: walking, braking, gripping, writing. A problem: wear, heat, wasted energy.
  • Increase friction: treads, grips, rough surfaces. Reduce friction: oil, wheels, ball bearings, smooth surfaces.
Example

A box slides to the right. Which way does friction act?

Friction opposes motion

Answer: To the left.

Example

Why do we oil a door hinge?

Oil is a lubricant

It reduces friction

Answer: To reduce friction so it opens easily.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking friction acts in the same direction as the motion.
  • Thinking friction is always bad. We could not walk or brake without it.
  • Thinking smooth surfaces have more friction.
  • Changing the block and the surface at the same time in a friction test.

faq.a: A force between two surfaces in contact. It acts in the opposite direction to the motion and slows things down.
Yes. It lets us walk, grip things, write and stop bicycles. It can also be a problem because it wears things out and produces heat.
Use lubricants such as oil, smooth surfaces, wheels or ball bearings.

items.q: Can friction act on an object that is not moving?
c: Yes. It can stop an object on a slope from sliding.
items.e: A box resting on a ramp stays still because of friction.

items.q: What happens when you rub your hands together quickly?
c: They get warm because of friction.
items.e: Friction produces heat.

items.q: What does friction produce when two surfaces rub together?
items.e: Rubbing hands together makes them warm.

items.q: What is friction?

a force that only magnets have
a force that pulls objects towards the Earth

items.q: Which measures the force needed to pull an object?

items.q: Why do we slip on a wet floor?

items.q: Which surface usually gives more friction?

items.q: Why is it hard to walk on ice?
c: Ice is smooth, so there is very little friction to grip.

items.q: Why do the soles of shoes wear out?

items.q: In which direction does friction act on a moving object?
